title: Furthermore, Meghiya, a bhikkhu dwells energetic and strenuous, abandoning unwholesome states, arousing wholesome states, steadfast, resolute, not discarding the burden regarding wholesome states. This is…
content: Furthermore, Meghiya, a bhikkhu dwells energetic and strenuous, abandoning unwholesome states, arousing wholesome states, steadfast, resolute, not discarding the burden regarding wholesome states. This is the fourth quality, Meghiya, that leads to the maturity of the unripe liberation of mind. Furthermore, Meghiya, a bhikkhu has wisdom, possessing wisdom that penetrates arising and passing away, with the noble penetration leading to the complete destruction of suffering. This is the fifth quality, Meghiya, that leads to the maturity of the unripe liberation of mind.

title: Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu takes hold of the hem of my robe and follows right behind me, placing his feet where my feet have been,…
content:
Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu takes hold of the hem of my robe and follows right behind me, placing his feet where my feet have been, yet if he has craving for sensual pleasures, strong greed, a hateful mind, evil thoughts, forgetfulness, lack of clear comprehension, unconcentrated, with distracted mind and loose faculties — that one is far from me, and I am far from him. Why is that? That bhikkhu does not see the Dhamma. Not seeing the Dhamma, he does not see me.

Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu lives a hundred leagues away, yet if he has no craving for sensual pleasures, no strong greed, no hateful mind, no evil thoughts, is mindful, clearly comprehending, concentrated, one-pointed, with restrained faculties — that one is close to me, and I am close to him. Why is that? That bhikkhu sees the Dhamma. Seeing the Dhamma, he sees me.

Though one may follow at the heel,
But full of desire and discontent,
Behold such a person: truly far, far away,
Far between one with craving and one without,
Far between the calm and the uncalm,
Far between one with greed and one who has abandoned greed.

Having fully known the Dhamma,
The wise one who knows the Dhamma,
Like a windless lake, unshaken, calm.
Behold such a person: truly near, very near,
Near between one without craving and one without craving,
Near between the calm and the calmed,
Near between the non-greedy and the one who has abandoned greed.

title: Elder Nāgasamāla: Adorned, wearing fine clothes, wearing garlands, fragrant, With sandalwood scent, in the crowd, on the main road, A dancer was dancing, moving to…
content:
Elder Nāgasamāla:

Adorned, wearing fine clothes, wearing garlands, fragrant,
With sandalwood scent, in the crowd, on the main road,
A dancer was dancing, moving to the music.

I entered the city for alms, passing by, I saw her —
Adorned, wearing fine clothes, setting the snare of death.

Then I reflected wisely, arousing right thought.
The danger appeared; disgusted, I became established.

And my mind was liberated — such is the Dhamma-nature.
I have attained the three knowledges; done is the Buddha's teaching.

title: Elder Bhadda: I was an only child, loved by father and mother. Through many rites and observances, I was obtained with entreaties. Out of compassion…
content:
Elder Bhadda:

I was an only child, loved by father and mother.
Through many rites and observances, I was obtained with entreaties.

Out of compassion for me, wishing for my happiness,
Both my father and mother led me to the Buddha.

'This son of ours, obtained with great difficulty,
Raised with delicacy, nurtured and cared for,
We respectfully offer him to you, O savior,
To serve as your attendant, to serve the conqueror.'

The Teacher accepted me, saying to Ānanda:
'Let him go forth; he will become virtuous.'

After the Teacher had me go forth,
The conqueror then entered the monastery.
Before the sun rose, my mind was liberated.

Then my Teacher, to complete the task,
From silent meditation, stood up and called me:
'Come, Bhadda.' Thus I received full ordination.

From birth, at seven years, I received full ordination.
I have attained the three knowledges — O Dhamma, good Dhamma-nature!

title: Just as rust is born from iron, And, born, eats away the iron, So excessive gain and honor lead One's own deeds to a bad…
content:
Just as rust is born from iron,
And, born, eats away the iron,
So excessive gain and honor lead
One's own deeds to a bad destination.

Among these defilements,
Ignorance is the worst.
Bhikkhu, abandon that defilement,
Become free from defilements.

Easy is life for the shameless,
One who is bold as a crow,
One who is backbiting and boastful,
One who is reckless and defiled.

Difficult is life for the modest,
One who always seeks purity,
One who is unassuming and humble,
One who is pure and bright.

title: There are these three kinds of persons, bhikkhus, who appear in the world. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a person accumulates harmful bodily formations, accumulates harmful…
content: There are these three kinds of persons, bhikkhus, who appear in the world. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a person accumulates harmful bodily formations, accumulates harmful verbal formations, accumulates harmful mental formations. Having accumulated harmful bodily formations, harmful verbal formations, harmful mental formations, he is reborn in a harmful world. Being reborn in a harmful world, harmful contacts touch him. Touched by harmful contacts, he experiences harmful feelings, exclusively painful, like beings in hell. Here, bhikkhus, a person accumulates non-harmful bodily formations ... non-harmful mental formations. Having accumulated non-harmful bodily formations ... non-harmful mental formations, he is reborn in a non-harmful world. Being reborn in a non-harmful world, non-harmful contacts touch him. Touched by non-harmful contacts, he experiences non-harmful feelings, exclusively pleasant, like the Subhakiṇha devas. Here, bhikkhus, a person accumulates both harmful and non-harmful bodily formations ... both harmful and non-harmful mental formations. Having accumulated both harmful and non-harmful bodily formations ... both harmful and non-harmful mental formations, he is reborn in a world that is both harmful and non-harmful. Being reborn in a world that is both harmful and non-harmful, contacts that are both harmful and non-harmful touch him. Touched by them, he experiences feelings that are both harmful and non-harmful, a mixture of pleasure and pain, like humans, some devas, and some beings in the lower realms. These three kinds of persons, bhikkhus, appear in the world.

title: Hard to find in the world is a person Who feels shame, who restrains himself, Who avoids reproach, Like a good horse avoids the whip.…
content:
Hard to find in the world is a person
Who feels shame, who restrains himself,
Who avoids reproach,
Like a good horse avoids the whip.

Like a good horse touched by the whip,
Be ardent and energetic.
With faith, virtue, and energy,
Concentration and investigation of states,
Endowed with clear knowledge and conduct, mindful,
Abandon this boundless suffering.

Irrigators guide water,
Fletchers shape arrows,
Carpenters shape wood,
The wise tame themselves.

title: Standing to one side, the devata Siva spoke this verse before the Blessed One: Associate with the good, Be close to the virtuous, Knowing the…
content:
Standing to one side, the devata Siva spoke this verse before the Blessed One:

Associate with the good,
Be close to the virtuous,
Knowing the good Dhamma from the wise,
One only becomes better, not worse.
Associate with the good,
Be close to the virtuous,
Knowing the good Dhamma from the wise,
One gains wisdom, not otherwise.
Associate with the good,
Be close to the virtuous,
Knowing the good Dhamma from the wise,
One does not sorrow amidst sorrow.
Associate with the good,
Be close to the virtuous,
Knowing the good Dhamma from the wise,
One shines among relatives.
Associate with the good,
Be close to the virtuous,
Knowing the good Dhamma from the wise,
Beings are reborn in good destinations.
Associate with the good,
Be close to the virtuous,
Knowing the good Dhamma from the wise,
Beings always enjoy happiness.

title: Elder Talapuṭa (continued): Develop jhāna, faculties, powers, Develop concentration, factors of enlightenment, Realize the three knowledges in the Buddha's teaching. O mind, encourage me, advise…
content:
Elder Talapuṭa (continued):

Develop jhāna, faculties, powers,
Develop concentration, factors of enlightenment,
Realize the three knowledges in the Buddha's teaching.
O mind, encourage me, advise me as before.

Develop the path to attain the Deathless,
The path leading to the penetration
Where all suffering is destroyed.
The eightfold path washing away all defilements —
O mind, encourage me, advise me as before.

Contemplate the aggregates as suffering,
Abandon from you the causes of suffering.
In this very life, make an end of suffering.
O mind, encourage me, advise me as before.

Contemplate with wisdom: impermanent, suffering,
Empty, not-self, evil, murderous,
Restrain your mind, do not let it run.
O mind, encourage me, advise me as before.

Shaven-headed and ugly, going about reviled,
When begging alms from families, holding a skull-shaped bowl —
Now are you focused on the Teacher's instruction,
The word of the great seer? O mind, encourage me, advise me as before.

Walk on the path with self well tamed,
Among houses, with mind not attached to sensual desires,
Like the full moon without a cloud.
O mind, encourage me, advise me as before.

Live in the forest, eat almsfood,
Dwell in a charnel ground, wear dust-heap robes,
Always sitting, never lying down,
Delight in the ascetic practices.
O mind, encourage me, advise me as before.

title: And, bhikkhus, what is dwelling in heedfulness? One who lives restraining the eye faculty, bhikkhus, his mind is not stained by forms cognizable by the…
content: And, bhikkhus, what is dwelling in heedfulness? One who lives restraining the eye faculty, bhikkhus, his mind is not stained by forms cognizable by the eye. For one with an unstained mind, gladness arises. With gladness, rapture arises. With rapture, the body becomes tranquil. With a tranquil body, he experiences happiness. For one who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated. With concentration, phenomena become manifest. When phenomena are manifest, that person is called one who dwells in heedfulness. ... the ear faculty ... the nose faculty ... the tongue faculty ... the body faculty ... One who lives restraining the mind faculty, his mind is not stained by mind-objects cognizable by the mind. For one with an unstained mind, gladness arises. With gladness, rapture arises. With rapture, the body becomes tranquil. With a tranquil body, he experiences happiness. For one who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated. With concentration, phenomena become manifest. When phenomena are manifest, that person is called one who dwells in heedfulness. Thus, bhikkhus, is dwelling in heedfulness.
